This differs from the other clusters because the focus is malware-like alerts and unwanted security software rather than account, operating system, or productivity software access.
examples: Remove recurring McAfee and resolve or reinstall problematic software
Computer locked by suspected scam virus with persistent alarm
Laptop blocked by fake Windows security pop-up warnings
Resolve Windows S mode preventing McAfee software access
Uninstall expired McAfee trial repeatedly prompting

clusters.name: Set up and register a new computer
clusters.description: Customers seek help getting a newly purchased computer ready for personal use, including initial setup and product registration. This differs from factory-reset requests because the goal is configuring a new device rather than restoring it.
examples: Set up newly purchased computer
Get help setting up new laptop correctly
Help setting up new laptop
Arrange in-home setup support for newly purchased desktop
Register a newly purchased laptop

clusters.name: Replace laptop after repeated repair failures
clusters.description: Customers seek replacement or refund after multiple unsuccessful repairs, recurring shutdowns, crashes, or unresolved hardware problems. The defining factor is repeated repair failure rather than simply preferring replacement for a new or unrepaired device.
examples: Replace laptop due to repeated unresolved hardware problems
Replace laptop after repeated unsuccessful repairs
Replace laptop that keeps shutting down after previous repair
Replace laptop with repeated blue screens and complete crash
Replace recently purchased laptop at no cost

clusters.name: Escalate unresolved repair or warranty case
clusters.description: Customers primarily want a supervisor or senior manager to address unresolved repair or warranty concerns. A few requests involve contacting a prior representative, obtaining a customer number, or purchasing software support.
examples: Escalate unresolved repair case to a senior manager
Speak with a supervisor about unresolved repair support
Speak with a manager about unresolved repair and warranty concerns
Escalate warranty dispute to a supervisor
Connect with previous support representative about ongoing driver issue

clusters.name: Keyboard backlight failure and settings
clusters.description: Customers report keyboard lighting that does not work, is uneven, or stops intermittently, and ask how to adjust brightness or color. All requests concern keyboard backlight operation or configuration rather than general keyboard key failures.
examples: Keyboard backlight stopped working
Turn on keyboard backlight that stopped working
Keyboard backlight not working on newly delivered laptop
Keyboard backlight is uneven and intermittently stops working
Laptop backlight LED remains nonfunctional after factory reset

clusters.name: Dock monitor and power dropouts
clusters.description: Customers report a dock intermittently or consistently failing to detect monitors, provide adequate laptop power, or maintain charging and display connections. One request mentions phantom inputs, but most concern display and power behavior through a dock.
examples: Dock does not detect external monitors or provide enough laptop power
Second monitor intermittently loses signal through USB-C dock adapter
Resolve low-voltage issue when desktop is docked to monitor
Docking station intermittently loses monitors and laptop charging
Dock is not detecting connected monitors

clusters.name: Bluetooth headphones or speakers lack audio
clusters.description: Customers report Bluetooth audio devices that fail to connect, disconnect, power on, or produce sound. Most requests concern wireless headphones or speakers, distinguishing this cluster from general speaker output and microphone issues.
examples: Bluetooth headphones connect but produce no sound
Audio not working on camera and Bluetooth headphones
Bluetooth speaker disconnects without playing audio on Chromebook
Bluetooth radio cannot connect devices
Headphones no longer work or power on

clusters.name: Hinge-related screen detachment damage
clusters.description: Customers report hinge damage accompanied by a detached, cracked, or nonresponsive screen, or separation between the display and the laptop base. This cluster is distinct from hinge-only repairs because the hinge failure has caused broader screen or casing separation.
examples: Laptop hinge popped out and screen is detached
Repair laptop hinge and damaged screen after a drop
Laptop screen cracked when closing, possibly due to hinge pressure
Repair laptop hinge damaged by a drop
Laptop screen detached from casing on first opening

clusters.name: Severe laptop slowness and lag
clusters.description: Customers call about very slow booting, browsing, application use, downloads, or overall system performance, sometimes worsening after extended use or software changes. Most requests concern broad laptop slowness, with a few focused specifically on internet download speed.
examples: Laptop's internet browsing is extremely slow and websites take minutes to load
Laptop is extremely slow and takes minutes to load Windows
Laptop runs slowly when opening applications and connecting to client network
Laptop experiences severe lag and sudden speed changes
Laptop becomes extremely slow after hours of use

clusters.name: Loud fan and general overheating
clusters.description: Customers call about excessively loud fan operation, device heat, and sometimes reduced performance during normal use. Unlike the other fan clusters, these requests generally seek diagnosis of noisy or hot operation without a clearly reported fan failure or mechanical buzzing.
examples: Laptop fan is loud and device overheats
Laptop fan is excessively loud during operation
Laptop fan makes excessive noise
Laptop overheats with loud fans and slow performance
Laptop fan makes a loud noise

clusters.name: Power failure after prior repair
clusters.description: Customers say the laptop still will not power on or work after a depot, warranty, or other prior repair. The defining feature is recurrence or persistence of the problem following repair service.
examples: Laptop still won't power on after repair
Laptop will not power on after recent repair
Laptop still will not power on after depot repair
Laptop won't start again after prior repair
Laptop will not power on and needs repair options

clusters.name: Recover or replace failed hard drive
clusters.description: Customers report a crashed or inaccessible hard drive and ask about recovering files, replacing the drive, or obtaining related recovery information. This cluster is centered on hard-drive failure and non-booting systems rather than routine backup or creating recovery media.
examples: Recover files from failed laptop hard drive
Laptop hard drive crashed and cannot access Windows
Replace failed laptop hard drive
Obtain recovery media for the laptop
Recover pictures from failed hard drive

clusters.name: Storage drive and memory not detected
clusters.description: Customers report startup or usability problems caused by undetected storage drives or incorrect or unavailable memory. This differs from Cluster 17 because these calls concern hardware detection and memory behavior rather than upgrade compatibility or feature guidance.
examples: Laptop cannot find hard drive during startup
Storage drive detection errors interrupt computer use
Secondary hard drive is not detected by laptop
Desktop cannot detect hard drive after initial setup
Laptop stuck retraining RAM during startup

clusters.name: Operating system activation, edition, and S mode
clusters.description: Customers need help with operating system activation, missing or incorrect edition licenses, identifying the original license, or leaving restricted S mode. This differs from the update cluster because the issue is licensing or software restrictions after or independent of updating.
examples: Windows 11 is not activated and no product key is found
Identify the original Windows version and activation license
Windows reinstalls as Home instead of purchased Pro edition
Windows remains in S mode and cannot download non-Microsoft apps
Verify Windows Pro license is included with new laptop

clusters.name: Activate or manage warranty renewal
clusters.description: Customers report problems activating, reinstating, or registering purchased or renewed warranty coverage, along with a renewal payment page or auto-renewal request. This differs from status inquiries because the customer needs an activation or account-management action.
examples: Activate purchased warranty renewal coverage
Activate pending warranty registration
Reinstate expired warranty coverage
Resolve delayed activation of purchased extended warranty
Disable auto-renewal for warranty plan on an old product

clusters.name: Warranty extension pricing and terms
clusters.description: Customers ask about the cost, payment terms, validity period, reinstatement fees, and recognition of warranty extensions or upgrades. The defining issue is purchasing or reinstating additional coverage.
examples: Ask about warranty extension pricing and available terms
Ask about warranty extension pricing and current issue coverage
Ask about warranty upgrade payment terms
Ask how long warranty upgrade pricing remains valid
Explain the $22 warranty reinstatement fee and extension terms

clusters.name: Warranty repair eligibility and charges
clusters.description: Customers seek to confirm that a repair is covered, whether diagnostic or labor charges apply, what information is needed, or how to start a warranty repair. This cluster focuses on initiating and validating a repair under existing coverage.
examples: Confirm warranty coverage and potential repair charges
Confirm warranty coverage and required information for authorized repair
Confirm repair will not incur warranty charges
Confirm warranty coverage and no support charges
Start a warranty repair

clusters.name: Check coverage for accidental damage repairs
clusters.description: Customers ask whether repairs are covered after drops, liquid damage, severe physical damage, hacking, crashes, or other specific incidents. The defining feature is coverage for damage or an incident rather than routine warranty status.
examples: Check warranty coverage for crashed laptop repair
Check warranty coverage for hacked laptop
Check warranty coverage for liquid-damaged laptop
Confirm accidental damage coverage after laptop was dropped again
Check warranty coverage for keyboard repair service

clusters.name: Replace recently purchased laptop
clusters.description: Customers ask to replace a newly purchased or malfunctioning laptop, obtain a newer replacement, or address a physical defect present since purchase. These requests focus on replacement of a recent purchase, including purchases from a retailer, rather than failed warranty repairs.
examples: Replace recently purchased laptop instead of repairing it
Replace laptop that has malfunctioned since purchase
Purchase a replacement laptop
Replace laptop purchased from Walmart
Purchase newer laptop with faster delivery

clusters.name: Find authorized local repair provider
clusters.description: Customers seek a nearby authorized repair center or want to arrange covered service through a local provider. Some also ask about repair estimates or reimbursement for local repairs, distinguishing this cluster from requests to replace the computer or correct its identifiers.
examples: Find nearby authorized repair provider
Arrange covered repair through an authorized local facility
Find nearest authorized repair center
Find authorized local warranty service for computer repair
Get repair cost estimate before approving service

clusters.name: Update customer account contact information
clusters.description: Customers primarily request changes to account details such as address, phone number, or email. A few requests concern email administration, server alerts, or obtaining a repair shipping label, making this cluster less focused.
examples: Update account address, phone number, and email
Email deletion checkbox does not respond consistently
Update repair case with alternative cell phone number
Delete thousands of emails more quickly
Configure SMTP email alerts on server

clusters.name: Follow up on existing support case
clusters.description: Customers seek assistance or callbacks for an already opened support, repair, or order case. This is broader than the technician-specific coordination in cluster 89 and less focused on status tracking than cluster 26.
examples: Follow up on existing ticket and technician callback
Get assistance with existing onsite repair case
Follow up on existing onsite support ticket for unresolved power issue
Follow up on existing repair and schedule fan replacement
Check status of existing technical support case

clusters.name: Existing repair status and technician scheduling
clusters.description: Customers primarily want updates on an open repair or replacement case, including technician visit timing and delivery status. This cluster is more narrowly focused on monitoring and scheduling already-created repair cases.
examples: Check status of existing laptop repair and technician visit
Check status of existing laptop repair
Check status and schedule technician visit for existing laptop repair
Check status of pending laptop replacement
Check status of two computers sent for repair

clusters.name: Device will not power on or charge
clusters.description: Customers report Chromebooks, laptops, or a tablet that will not turn on, show charging, or respond after charging and reset attempts. The cluster is focused on complete power or charging failure rather than battery runtime.
examples: Chromebook won't turn on and power light keeps blinking
Chromebook won't power on after charging and reset attempts
Chromebook won't turn on and needs warranty service
Laptop will not power on or charge
Chromebook shows no charging indicator when plugged in

clusters.name: Sudden shutdown and power failure
clusters.description: Customers report that the laptop suddenly stopped working, shut down, or became unable to power on, including after an update or before reaching network access. The cluster is distinguished by the sudden onset or shutdown context rather than a persistent no-indicator condition.
examples: Laptop won't power on
Laptop suddenly stopped powering on
Laptop suddenly shut down and will not power on
Laptop will not turn on or do anything
Laptop won't power on after system update

clusters.name: Charging failure despite replacement chargers
clusters.description: Customers report that the computer does not recognize chargers, show a charging indicator, charge the battery, or power on even after trying multiple or replacement chargers. It is broader than the other charging clusters and includes a tablet charging issue.
examples: Laptop is not charging and shows no charging indicator
Laptop won't power on or charge despite replacement charger
Laptop stopped working, possibly battery or charging failure
Laptop does not recognize charger or charge battery
Laptop battery is not charging with multiple USB-C chargers

clusters.name: Sleep, wake, or unexpected power cycling
clusters.description: Customers report problems entering sleep, waking from sleep, or unexpectedly waking and powering on. This differs from general crashes because the issue is tied specifically to sleep and lid-close behavior.
examples: Laptop intermittently fails to wake from sleep
Laptop cannot wake from sleep unless replugged
Laptop intermittently fails to wake after closing lid
Laptop cycles repeatedly between sleep and wake
Laptop won't enter sleep mode

clusters.name: Black screen triggered by login, movement, or video
clusters.description: Customers report the display going black after Windows appears, immediately after login, when the lid or display is moved, or while video applications are open. These are usage- or transition-triggered blackouts rather than a continuously blank screen or primarily power-related failure.
examples: Laptop screen goes black during startup and use
Laptop screen goes black after Windows screen appears
Laptop screen goes black after entering password
Screen goes black when laptop display is opened or rotated
Screen goes black immediately after logging in

clusters.name: Wi-Fi driver installation after Windows reinstall
clusters.description: Customers need to restore Wi-Fi or install the wireless driver after reinstalling or clean-installing Windows, often without an active internet connection. These requests focus on driver availability and setup rather than defective hardware or intermittent connectivity.
examples: Reinstall missing Wi-Fi driver after Windows reinstall
Install Wi-Fi driver after Windows reinstall without network connection
Troubleshoot Wi-Fi connection by reinstalling the laptop driver
Wi-Fi adapter disabled and drivers cannot be installed after OS reinstall
Wi-Fi unavailable during clean Windows installation

clusters.name: Create or obtain Windows recovery media
clusters.description: Customers need a Windows recovery USB or factory recovery image, or encounter errors while creating or using recovery media to reinstall the operating system. Unlike Cluster 105, the main issue is the recovery media or reinstallation process, not a failed hard drive.
examples: Create Windows recovery USB for laptop that will not boot
Purchase USB recovery drive to reinstall Windows
Purchase Windows recovery media after creation repeatedly fails
Operating system recovery fails with preload error from USB drive
Cannot access Lenovo ID to create USB recovery media

clusters.name: Screen brightness controls not working
clusters.description: Customers report that the display stays dim, changes brightness incorrectly, or ignores brightness-key and monitor controls. This cluster focuses specifically on malfunctioning brightness adjustment rather than general display problems.
examples: Screen brightness changes incorrectly when adjusting brightness
Screen brightness will not increase using brightness keys
Screen brightness becomes dark after every restart
Laptop screen remains dim despite maximum brightness settings
Monitor brightness controls do not work

clusters.name: Language-specific support connection requests
clusters.description: Customers ask to connect with support or sales representatives speaking French, Spanish, or English, with one broader software-support connection request. This concerns reaching an appropriate language or support line, rather than transferring an active call between departments.
examples: Connect with a French-speaking support agent
Speak with a French-language support representative
Connect with English-speaking sales support
Request Spanish-language technical support
Reach software support for assistance

clusters.name: Support phone number or eligibility information
clusters.description: Customers seek the correct support phone number, phone menu, or confirmation that they qualify for a support service, with one request to reconnect to a prior representative. This cluster is primarily about finding or validating the right access route rather than requesting an active department transfer.
examples: Get phone number for Premier Support
Get correct support number for technician service
Confirm eligibility for Premier Support assistance
Find correct phone menu for Ultimate Care support
Reconnect with the previous support representative after disconnected call

clusters.name: Purchase additional warranty coverage
clusters.description: Customers want to buy an extended or upgraded warranty for one or more devices, often while limited coverage remains. This cluster focuses on purchasing added protection rather than checking status or resolving activation problems.
examples: Purchase extended warranty coverage for the laptop
Extend or upgrade laptop warranty coverage
Purchase additional warranty for laptop with limited remaining coverage
Extend warranty coverage for both laptops before expiration
Activate or extend warranty for Chromebook

clusters.name: Warranty duration, region, and hardware coverage
clusters.description: Customers ask about warranty length, coverage by purchase region, and whether hardware problems such as power or charging failures are covered. It is distinguished by questions about geographic scope, duration, and basic hardware-failure eligibility.
examples: Check warranty coverage for US-purchased laptop
Check laptop warranty duration and coverage
Check international warranty coverage for planned laptop purchase
Confirm laptop warranty coverage for power failure
Check warranty coverage for laptop charging problem

clusters.name: Out-of-warranty repair options
clusters.description: Customers ask about paid repair availability, costs, or warranty-status corrections for computers outside coverage. This cluster is defined by repair eligibility after warranty expiration rather than a specific hardware symptom.
examples: Check repair options for out-of-warranty laptop
Ask about paid repair options for an out-of-warranty desktop
Correct incorrect out-of-warranty status for refurbished laptop
Repair crashed desktop that is outside warranty
Repair laptop battery, trackpad, and backlight problems

clusters.name: No-boot or no-power repair service
clusters.description: Customers need repair for laptops or desktops that will not boot, start, or turn on, usually under warranty. It is distinguished from other repair clusters by the prominent no-start symptom.
examples: Laptop stopped working and needs warranty repair
Laptop won't boot and needs repair service
Resolve laptop no-boot issue under warranty
ThinkPad won't boot and needs out-of-warranty paid repair
Desktop will not turn on and needs warranty repair

clusters.name: Coordinate onsite technician repair
clusters.description: Customers call about missed technician callbacks, rescheduling appointments, restarting technician work, or understanding closure of an onsite repair case. The defining feature is direct coordination with a field technician or onsite work order.
examples: Resume on-hold repair and coordinate technician contact
Follow up on missed technician callback for laptop service
Get field technician support for existing desktop work order
Reschedule onsite technician appointment for tomorrow
Understand why existing repair case was closed

clusters.name: Fan failure causing overheating and shutdown
clusters.description: Customers report extreme CPU overheating, fan failure alerts or nonfunctioning fans, severe slowdown, and unexpected shutdowns. This cluster centers on critical thermal failure rather than ordinary fan noise.
examples: Laptop overheats, fan runs wildly, and hard reset is required
Laptop overheats and shuts down because the fan may not run
Laptop overheats and shuts off after several minutes
Computer reports CPU fan failure and runs extremely slowly
CPU temperature reaches 100 degrees after motherboard replacement

clusters.name: Fan buzzing or rattling needing repair
clusters.description: Customers report unusual buzzing or rattling from the fan and often ask for expedited repair or warranty coverage. A few requests involve fan errors, overheating, crashes, or failure to boot, making this somewhat broader than the primary noise complaint.
examples: Expedite repair for laptop fan making buzzing noise
Laptop fan makes buzzing and rattling noises
Check warranty coverage for laptop fan making unusual noise
Laptop won't boot because of a fan error
Laptop crashes and overheats during gaming

clusters.name: Desktop powers on with no display
clusters.description: Customers report a desktop or all-in-one that powers on but produces no monitor image or video signal, sometimes with beeps or a black screen. This cluster focuses on complete loss of video output rather than display distortion or intermittent blackouts.
examples: Desktop powers on but produces no display or beeps
Desktop tower powers on but shows no monitor display
Desktop boots but produces no video signal
Desktop won't power on and shows black screen after boot
All-in-one display flashes white and shows no video

clusters.name: Intermittent black screen tied to power or startup
clusters.description: Customers report black screens that recur depending on charger connection, unplugging, startup errors, or similar power-related conditions. This differs from blackouts triggered by login, opening or rotating the display, or video applications.
examples: Laptop screen intermittently turns black
Laptop intermittently blacks out unless charger is connected
Laptop shows recurring KMODE exception black screen at startup
Desktop powers on but screen stays blank until unplugged
Browser videos keep spinning and will not play

clusters.name: Internet connectivity stopped or unavailable
clusters.description: Customers report that the laptop cannot access the internet through Wi-Fi or Ethernet, including cases where Wi-Fi appears to work. This is a broad internet-access problem rather than a request focused on connecting to a particular network or fixing the wireless adapter.
examples: Laptop cannot connect to the internet
Cannot connect to internet despite working Wi-Fi
Laptop cannot find available home Wi-Fi network
Ethernet port does not connect to wired internet
Legion Go Wi-Fi stopped working

clusters.name: Tablet locked by forgotten PIN or account
clusters.description: Customers cannot access a tablet because of a forgotten PIN, a previous owner's account, or a lock triggered after resetting the device. The stolen-device tracking request is an outlier, but most requests concern tablet access and account locks.
examples: Tablet locked out after password or PIN entry
Cannot access tablet after forgotten password and corruption message
Forgot previous PIN required after factory resetting tablet
Remove previous owner's account and PIN from tablet
Track or remotely disable stolen tablet to protect stored information

clusters.name: Recover or reinstall Windows without BitLocker key
clusters.description: Customers are trying to regain access, recover files, reset the laptop, or reinstall Windows when the BitLocker recovery key is unavailable. This is distinct from recurring BitLocker prompts and from key retrieval tied to hardware replacement.
examples: Recover BitLocker-locked laptop without a Microsoft recovery key
Recover BitLocker key to regain access to Windows
Recover files from BitLocker-locked laptop
Reset laptop and reinstall Windows without BitLocker recovery key
Windows reinstall fails after BitLocker recovery attempt

clusters.name: Check accidental damage warranty coverage
clusters.description: Customers ask whether accidental physical damage, battery issues, or device replacement are covered, or whether an accidental coverage purchase is active. The defining topic is the scope and status of accidental damage protection.
examples: Check warranty coverage for accidental physical damage
Determine whether accidental damage coverage provides replacement
Check status of accidental coverage purchase
Clarify battery, hardware, and physical damage warranty coverage

clusters.name: Repair logistics after warranty purchase
clusters.description: Customers ask about repair return shipping, diagnostic fee treatment, or canceling a repair after obtaining or using warranty coverage. It differs by focusing on the practical handling of a repair after a warranty purchase or repair request, rather than initial coverage verification.
examples: Confirm warranty coverage and repair eligibility after warranty purchase
Clarify warranty repair return shipping charges
Cancel existing warranty repair after charging issue resolved
Whether diagnostic fee is applied toward repair cost

clusters.name: Verify warranty coverage and recurring charges
clusters.description: Customers want to validate warranty status, reconcile conflicting coverage information, or understand a recurring service payment. It differs from general warranty-status questions through its emphasis on discrepancies and billing-related coverage.
examples: Validate warranty coverage for Lenovo computer
Verify discrepancy between Lenovo and Best Buy warranty coverage
Verify laptop warranty coverage
Identify recurring Lenovo service payment and coverage

clusters.name: External display cable or port failure
clusters.description: Customers report missing video or a failed cable or display port when connecting a monitor or television. It is distinct from the broader monitor setup cluster because these requests focus on a nonworking connection, with one unrelated screenshot request as an outlier.
examples: External monitor lacks video when laptop powers on through USB-C dock
Replace nonworking USB-C monitor cable
HDMI port stopped working with television
Learn how to take screenshots using Windows snipping tools

clusters.name: Replacement motherboard installation defects
clusters.description: Customers report problems with replacement system boards, such as failed memory slots, undetected graphics hardware, short risers, or damage causing no power. This cluster concerns replacement-board fit, compatibility, or component functionality rather than general motherboard failure.
examples: Replacement system board has a nonworking memory slot and won't boot
GPU is not detected after motherboard replacement
Replace burned motherboard and LCD cable causing no power
Replacement motherboard has short risers preventing heat sink installation

clusters.name: Transfer files and programs to new computer
clusters.description: Customers want to move files, applications, or software from an old computer to a new one. This differs from general new-computer setup because the main need is migration of existing data and programs.
examples: Transfer files and applications to another laptop
Transfer software and programs from previous computer
Transfer files and save them correctly on new laptop
Transfer files from old tower to new desktop

clusters.name: Restore computer to factory settings
clusters.description: Customers want to return a computer or tablet to its factory state, including after setup or login problems. This differs from new-computer setup because it involves resetting an existing configuration rather than establishing one.
examples: Restore laptop to factory settings for personal setup
Restore computer to factory settings without removing Windows
Restore new laptop to factory settings after setup login problem
Restore tablet to factory settings
